ov: A forest animal of the north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, also called the forest giraffe. Despite the zebra-like stripes on its legs, its closest relative is the giraffe. Its coat is chocolate to reddish brown, and it lives alone, meeting others only to breed.
rg: North-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
df: Tree leaves and buds, branches, grasses, ferns, fruits and fungi: over 100 plant species, some of them poisonous to humans.

cf.tip: The okapi is the giraffe’s only living relative.
Despite the striped legs, the okapi isn’t related to zebras.

fx: Males have short, horn-like bumps on the head, like a giraffe’s.
Pregnancy lasts about 440–450 days, and usually a single calf is born.
